findings.summary: is_near_duplicate uses `<=` instead of `>=`, inverting the near-duplicate check.
findings.mechanism: The task requires reporting true when cosine similarity meets or exceeds the threshold. The implementation returns `_cosine(e1, e2) <= threshold`, so identical vectors (cosine=1.0) with threshold=0.95 would evaluate 1.0 <= 0.95 = False, incorrectly reporting them as NOT near-duplicates, while low-similarity or orthogonal vectors (cosine=0.0) evaluate 0.0 <= 0.95 = True, incorrectly reporting them AS near-duplicates. This is the exact opposite of intended behavior and would pass unrelated records as duplicates while missing true near-duplicates.
